issues.legal_issue: General limitation provisions apply to an appeal under a special enactment when that enactment does not exclude them, and a discretionary order condoning delay should not be disturbed where no basis for interference is shown.
material_facts: An appeal against the compensation assessment was filed after the prescribed period.
The special enactment contained no provision excluding the applicable general limitation provisions.
The District Judge condoned the delay, considering the circumstances and the interests of justice.
The Supreme Court found no reason to interfere with that discretionary decision in its special-leave jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The general limitation provisions applied, the District Judge had power to condone the delay, and the Supreme Court declined to interfere with the exercise of that discretion.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 29(2) of the Limitation Act, 1963, sections 4 to 24 apply to proceedings under a special enactment unless that enactment excludes their application. The District Judge could therefore condone the delay; the Supreme Court found no basis to disturb that discretionary decision under Article 136 of the Constitution.

rule.if: appeal_under_special_enactment and appeal_filed_late and special_enactment_does_not_exclude_general_limitation and lower_court_condoned_delay and lower_court_relied_on_justice_and_fairness

predicates.appeal_under_special_enactment: A party brought an appeal under a special enactment against an administrative determination.
predicates.appeal_filed_late: The party filed the appeal after the applicable filing period had expired.
predicates.special_enactment_does_not_exclude_gener: The special enactment contains no rule excluding the general limitation provisions that permit extension or exclusion of time.
predicates.lower_court_condoned_delay: The court hearing the appeal allowed it to proceed despite its late filing.
predicates.lower_court_relied_on_justice_and_fairne: The court hearing the appeal relied on the circumstances and the interests of justice and fairness in allowing the late appeal.

issues.definition: When a late appeal under a special enactment is not barred from relying on general limitation provisions and the lower court condones the delay on justice-and-fairness grounds, the condonation is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A surcharge imposed on land revenue forms part of annual land revenue when calculating compensation by reference to that revenue.
material_facts: Land was acquired as excess land under a land-ceiling scheme, and compensation was calculated by reference to a multiple of the annual land revenue payable for it.
The surcharge was imposed as a percentage of land revenue and was an enhancement of that revenue.
The surcharge was assessed and collected in addition to, or along with, land revenue; those arrangements did not change its nature.
issues.conclusion: The surcharge constituted land revenue and had to be included in the annual land revenue used to assess compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the Assam Fixation of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1956 measures compensation by the full rate of annual land revenue payable for the acquired land. A surcharge is an additional imposition having the same nature as the tax on which it is imposed, so a surcharge on land revenue is an enhancement of land revenue. The Court relied on Bisra Stone Lime Co. Ltd. v. Orissa State Electricity Board, Commissioner of Income Tax, Kerala v. K. Srinivasan, and Vishwesha Thirthaswamiar v. State of Mysore; it also considered the definition of land revenue in section 3(e) of the Assam Land and Revenue Regulation, 1886, and the levy and recovery provisions of the Assam Land Revenue and Land (Surcharge) Act, 1970.

predicates.compensation_assessed_by_annual_land_rev: The proceeding determines compensation for acquired land by using the annual land revenue payable for that land as its measure.
predicates.surcharge_imposed_on_land_revenue: A surcharge is imposed as an additional charge on the land revenue payable for the land.
predicates.surcharge_has_same_nature_as_underlying_: The additional charge enhances the underlying land revenue rather than imposing a levy distinct from it.

issues.definition: If compensation is measured by annual land revenue and the surcharge enhances that revenue without changing its nature, the surcharge is included in the compensation basis.

issues.legal_issue: A local rate levied for specified local purposes is distinct from land revenue and is not included in compensation calculated by reference to annual land revenue.
material_facts: Compensation for acquired land was measured by reference to annual land revenue payable for it.
The local rate was levied on land to fund famine relief, famine prevention, and local purposes.
The governing provisions treated the rate as a cess and provided for its recovery as an arrear of land revenue, but did not make it land revenue.
issues.conclusion: The local rate was distinct from land revenue and had to be excluded from the compensation calculation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the Assam Fixation of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1956 uses annual land revenue as the compensation measure. A levy that is in the nature of a cess, is dedicated to specified purposes, and is merely recoverable as an arrear of land revenue remains distinct from land revenue. The Court relied on section 4 of the Assam Local Rates Regulation, 1879, Guruswamy & Co. v. State of Mysore, and India Cement Ltd. v. State of Tamil Nadu.

rule.if: compensation_assessed_by_annual_land_revenue and levy_is_a_local_rate and levy_funds_specified_local_purposes and levy_is_distinct_from_land_revenue

predicates.compensation_assessed_by_annual_land_rev: The proceeding determines compensation for acquired land by using the annual land revenue payable for that land as its measure.
predicates.levy_is_a_local_rate: A separate levy is imposed on land as a local rate or cess.
predicates.levy_funds_specified_local_purposes: The proceeds of the levy are assigned to particular local or relief purposes rather than forming part of general public revenue.
predicates.levy_is_distinct_from_land_revenue: The levy remains legally distinct from land revenue even if its amount is calculated by reference to land value or it is recoverable as an arrear of land revenue.

issues.definition: If compensation is measured by annual land revenue and a separate local levy funds specified purposes while remaining distinct from land revenue, that levy is excluded from the compensation basis.
